the garbage collector is a key component for energy optimization in an embedded environment, that a garbage collector-controlled leakage energy optimization is feasible and that the leakage optimization is effective for a variety of garbage collection schemes.
the garbage collector is a key component of the JVM for energy saving and that the GC-controlled leakage energy reduction technique can save 30% of the total energy consumption.
(1) the GC can be used to reduce energy consumption in an embedded Java system; and (2) the energy savings are significant, up to 50% for a specific embedded architecture.

tuning specific components of the Java virtual machine for energy saving.
a novel approach of tuning the JVM for energy saving.
the design, analysis, and tuning of the GC for energy-constrained environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GC is a critical part of an embedded JVM that can be used for energy saving.
the GC is a critical component for both memory-constrained and energy-constrained systems.
tuning garbage collection for energy saving in an embedded environment is possible, and that the tuning is a complex process that involves many parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the GC can be used to control the leakage power consumption of a memory system, and we have demonstrated the importance of the GC tuning for energy saving.
the energy saving can be as high as 40%, with only 1.2% performance degradation.
the GC is an important tool for energy optimization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the JVM should not only be tuned for performance but also for energy consumption.
the GC is an essential component of an energy-optimized embedded Java environment.
a GC-controlled leakage optimization technique can reduce the energy consumption of an embedded JVM by up to 40%.
